source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
After harvest, bunches intended for natural ripening are commonly stored in a shaded, covered container - the source shows bunches placed in a lined basket or clay jar covered with banana leaves - which traps the ethylene the fruit naturally produces and speeds even ripening. Ripening by this method typically takes a few days, and fruit is checked periodically for color change.

Careful handling throughout harvest, transport and storage matters because bruised or damaged fruit ripens unevenly, develops dark blemished patches, and sells for a lower price or becomes unsellable, so minimizing impact and pressure on the fruit at every stage protects the harvest's market value.
